messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Erro in part 5
parts:
Hi Andreas,

GGIR part 3 and 4 are by default designed to classify sleep based on 5 second epochs. For the alternative sleep algorithms such as Sadeh1994 GGIR is more flexible but there the challenge is that there are insufficient studies to evaluate validity. If you want to classify sleep at a different resolution you should first make sure that sleep detection is meaningful.

This is important, because part 5 heavily depends on meaningful sleep detection part 5.
This is why I implemented the argument part5_agg2_60seconds, which allows you to work with 5 second epochs for sleep but then to aggregate to 60 seconds. We could in theory enhance the code to allow for more aggregation resolutions, e.g. 10, 15, 30, and 60. Although that would require a bit of time investment (support in terms of helping to enhance the code or hiring me to work on this would be appreciated).

The flexibility to choose an epoch length via argument windowsizes was originally designed for part 2 only. For part 3, 4 and 5 it is probably best to stick with 5 seconds and then to consider aggregating to 60 seconds as described above.

Best,

Vincent
